verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {petitioner_name}, aged about {petitioner_age} years, resident of {petitioner_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above petition are true and correct to the best of my knowledge derived from personal experience and records. Matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner

promptInstructions: Draft a petition for appointment as guardian and grant of custody of minor under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (and/or Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 for Hindu minors).

PARAMOUNT PRINCIPLE: Welfare of the minor is the paramount consideration. Every section of the petition must orient toward welfare — physical, mental, moral, educational, emotional. Cite Gaurav Nagpal v. Sumedha Nagpal (2009) 1 SCC 42 and Nil Ratan Kundu v. Abhijit Kundu (2008) 9 SCC 413.
Identify the minor — name, date of birth, current age, gender, religion (relevant for HMGA), and place where minor ordinarily resides.

Status of natural guardians: For Hindu minor, S.6 HMGA — father is natural guardian and after him the mother. Per Githa Hariharan v. RBI (1999) 2 SCC 228, 'after' read as 'in absence of' — mother can act as natural guardian during father's lifetime in his absence or inability.
Plead the ground for petition: death of natural guardian / incapacity / unfitness / custody dispute / absence / welfare requirement.

Demonstrate petitioner's suitability per S.17 GWA factors: capacity to provide for minor, character, financial means, kinship to minor, religious affinity, age, sex (for protection), and any wishes of deceased parent.
If minor is of sufficient age (typically 9+ years) to form intelligent preference, mention minor's preference per S.17(3) GWA.
Identify whether guardianship of PERSON, PROPERTY, or both is sought. For property, give particulars of minor's property and proposed safeguards.

Jurisdiction under S.9 GWA — application must be made to District Court (or Family Court) of the place where minor ORDINARILY RESIDES. Not casual residence. Refer to Ruchi Majoo v. Sanjeev Majoo (2011) 6 SCC 479.
Disclose any prior proceedings — divorce, prior custody orders, foreign court orders.
If seeking interim custody, plead urgency and prima facie welfare basis.
Tone: child-centric. Avoid pejorative attacks on natural guardian unless legally necessary to plead unfitness — even then, factual and proportionate.
Note for advocate: Section 7 GWA — court can appoint guardian for welfare of minor. Section 19 GWA — court cannot appoint where father is living unless unfit.

sections.description: Power of court to make order as to guardianship — welfare of minor
Persons entitled to apply for order
Court having jurisdiction — where minor ordinarily resides
Matters to be considered by court in appointing guardian — welfare of minor; capacity, character, kinship, etc.
Restriction — where father is living and not unfit, court shall not appoint another guardian of minor
Title of guardian to custody of ward
Natural guardians of Hindu minor — father (and after him mother); for minor's exclusive property different rules apply for boy/unmarried girl vs married girl
Powers of natural guardian — alienation of property requires court permission
Welfare of minor to be paramount consideration in appointment of guardian

filing_checklist: Death certificate(s) of deceased natural guardian(s) (if applicable)
Identity and address proofs of petitioner
Income proof of petitioner (salary slips, ITRs, bank statements)
Medical records (if minor or guardian's health is in issue)
Photographs of minor with petitioner (cohabitation / care evidence)
Property documents (if guardianship of property sought)
Consent affidavit of minor (if minor is of age to give consent)
Newspaper notice as ordered (S.11 GWA procedure)
Court fee as per state schedule
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: minor_name and minor_dob must not be empty
minor_age_years must be consistent with minor_dob
natural_guardians_status, father_status and mother_status must not be empty
type_of_guardianship must contain at least one option
If governing_act is HMGA_1956_hindu, minor_religion should be Hindu (or Buddhist/Jain/Sikh per S.2 HMGA)
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Gaurav Nagpal v. Sumedha Nagpal (2009) 1 SCC 42 — welfare of child is paramount consideration; not parental rights
Nil Ratan Kundu v. Abhijit Kundu (2008) 9 SCC 413 — welfare doctrine; subjective satisfaction of court
Githa Hariharan v. RBI (1999) 2 SCC 228 — 'after' father in S.6 HMGA read as 'in absence of'; mother as natural guardian in father's lifetime
Ruchi Majoo v. Sanjeev Majoo (2011) 6 SCC 479 — 'ordinarily resides' interpretation; jurisdiction in inter-country custody
Roxann Sharma v. Arun Sharma (2015) 8 SCC 318 — custody of child below 5 ordinarily with mother (S.6(a) proviso HMGA)
Athar Hussain v. Syed Siraj Ahmed (2010) 2 SCC 654 — non-Hindu guardianship under GWA
Surinder Kaur Sandhu v. Harbax Singh Sandhu (1984) 3 SCC 698 — foreign court custody orders; welfare overrides
disclaimer: Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.
